quote: having to go it alone in the forests was probably a death sentence
content: Yudkowsky commendably flags this as speculation, but it is worth labeling plainly: an unfalsifiable just-so story. We have no measurement of the reproductive costs of solitary dissent in ancestral environments, and "the fear of thinking really different is stronger than the fear of death" is asserted from a single contrast (more people skydive than sign up for cryonics) that has simpler explanations, skydiving is socially legible and cryonics is widely regarded as implausible. There is genuine research on the pain of social exclusion (Eisenberger, Lieberman & Williams 2003 on "social pain"), but it does not establish an evolved module that ranks ostracism-avoidance above survival. The narrative is plausible-sounding decoration, not evidence.
